title: Produce units: capacity meter
description: The produce dialog shows the capacity of the system being built in, live as builds are staged: ships there, queued ships, and what needs it (fighters, ground forces placed in space). Orange when queued units would not fit; never blocks. Values come from the engine (details.capacity and per-option capacity_* fields). Synthetic mocked game.

shots.heading: No capacity yet, desktop
shots.caption: No ships in the system and nothing queued: Capacity 0 / 0.

shots.heading: A carrier queued raises capacity, desktop
shots.caption: One carrier and two fighters queued: the breakdown shows Queued ships +6 and the meter reads 4 / 6, still green.

shots.heading: Fighters over capacity, desktop
shots.caption: Capacity 8 / 4 with 4 fighters over: the meter and Build button turn alert orange, the fighter row is outlined with 'Over capacity: these would be removed'. Building is still allowed.

shots.heading: Arborec, system without a planet, desktop
shots.caption: Production in a system with no planet (space-area production): ground forces can only be placed in the space area, so the queued infantry count toward capacity (4 / 2, 2 units over).

notes.title: Source.
notes.text: Capacity of each ship, Carrier II, faction and technology modifiers, dock fighter support and the destination of produced units all come from the engine; the dialog only adds them up.

notes.title: Planetless systems.
notes.text: With no planet, the space area is the only destination, so produced ground forces count toward capacity (the engine reports space_placement always).

notes.title: Over capacity.
notes.text: Units over capacity are removed when production ends. Orange is a warning, not a block.
